feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear public-sector specialization and solid evidence of scope, progression, and technical breadth. It reads polished and substantive, but it is slightly repetitive, somewhat dense, and could sharpen impact by reducing overlap and adding more outcome-focused results.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo into senior ownership of web, analytics, governance, multimedia, and team operations.  
- Good credibility signals: specific platforms, scale metrics, and concrete projects make the experience feel real and senior-level.  
- Writing is generally polished and professional, with consistent tone and strong alignment between headline, skills, and experience.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to save space and improve structure.  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity/scope, e.g., traffic growth, engagement gains, efficiency improvements, adoption rates, or campaign results.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward; capitalization is inconsistent in “Coleman DAVIS” vs standard name styling; footer project descriptions are strong but formatted more like portfolio copy than CV content.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and public-sector focus, but it reads slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with sharper outcomes and a cleaner lead sentence.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and simplify: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct action language such as “leading modernization of” or “scaling.”
- Consider adding one concrete scope marker from recent roles, e.g., “10,000+ page websites,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ publishers,” to increase impact.
- Refine the second sentence to reduce list-like phrasing: “Combines web modernization, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled search to improve discovery, governance, and audience experience.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled search” would be more specific and consistent.
- The subtitle already signals leadership; avoid repeating “leader/leads” too prominently.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and weighted toward senior, recent strengths.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize phrasing for parallel structure; avoid mixing systems, functions, and sectors unevenly.
- Emphasize higher-level leadership areas over broad descriptors like “communications operations.”
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve more technical/platform-specific language for Topline Skills and Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled…,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” repeat language already used in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” also echoes multiple work experience bullets; keep only if targeting policy/public-sector roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots that reinforce the CV’s themes, but they read a bit dense and overlap with achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make the footer feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, punchier structure: “Project name: action + platform/format + purpose/outcome.”
- Add 1 concrete qualifier where possible (audience, scale, campaign type, or business goal), especially for the microsite and anniversary campaign.
- Trim technical stacking in “AI Hybrid Search” to improve readability: “hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content, and bill-level AI chat.”
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency and readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely repeat the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- Consider framing these as selected examples with distinct outcomes so they complement, rather than restate, the work history.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical range, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your NACo entries. Tighten it around the highest-value consulting outcomes, especially the AI search and Drupal/platform modernization work.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client value: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant to a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into sharper outcome-led lines: “Redesigned digital workflows, governance, and analytics to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Make the Drupal work more concise and specific: “Built campaign microsites, modular content components, and member-facing toolkits in Drupal; provided front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.”
- Keep the AI item, but make impact measurable if possible: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and discovery UX to improve findability.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats NACo language; use consulting-specific outcomes or scale instead.
- “Web, email, social, multimedia” is already well-covered elsewhere; don’t restate channel ownership unless tied to a result.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It would be sharper if the opening were less list-like and if each bullet emphasized outcomes, team leadership, and transformation rather than channel ownership alone.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget strategy for a national association serving county officials.”
- Tighten the website bullet: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Reframe channel management around impact: add metrics such as email engagement, audience growth, campaign performance, production volume, or cost/time savings if available.
- Combine operations/analytics/studio bullets into outcome-led statements, e.g., “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio and expanded analytics across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve reporting, content planning, and production capacity.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led digital communications across web, email, social media and video” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this role focused on enterprise leadership and modernization.
- Video growth also appears in earlier NACo roles; here, emphasize the studio build and organizational scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good channel breadth, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles. Make it more distinct by emphasizing operational leadership, editorial coordination, and advocacy content execution rather than broad digital ownership.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media, and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show outcome: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring channel for policy communications.”
- Strengthen workflow/editorial bullets: “Built stronger editorial planning across communications, advocacy, and program teams, improving publishing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “web, email, social media and video” and “publishing workflows” are repeated in the Director and prior NACo roles; keep this entry focused on execution/coordination, not platform oversight.
- “weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this one as scaling/formalizing the channel.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo bullets. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing enterprise leadership and governance rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, higher-signal wording such as:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Swap “audience-focused content planning” for “audience-centered content strategy” to sound more senior and outcome-oriented.
- Consider “content operations” instead of “editorial systems” to better match recent experience building workflows, governance, and enterprise publishing structures.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this area to scale/results rather than here; skills sections should stay concise.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” is very close to Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communication.”
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and governance language also repeat the header summary; keep this version more specialized.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s currently a mixed keyword list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. Make it more selective and impact-oriented, emphasizing the platforms and execution areas most supported by recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal • CMS modernization & migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations • Workflow automation • Airtable systems • AI-enabled search
- Prioritize Drupal and CMS modernization first, since recent roles show major Drupal build/migration work and AI search leadership.
- Remove lower-signal items unless they are central to target roles; “WordPress,” “SharePoint,” and “Power Pages” are less supported by recent experience here.
- Consider replacing generic “Technical Execution” phrasing with “Web Platforms, CMS Modernization & Technical Delivery” for stronger alignment to the work history.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills shorter and more strategic, with detailed tools left to the technical section.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with Core Competencies/Technical + IT, so only keep if they are differentiators for target roles.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for recent leadership roles, but the item reads like a generic keyword list. It would be stronger if grouped around business value and framed to reflect senior ownership of reporting, measurement, and optimization.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented capabilities, e.g.: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, and Microsoft Clarity for KPI frameworks, executive reporting, and digital performance analysis.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboards and decision support” or “Executive reporting and insight generation” for sharper phrasing.
- Consider changing “SEO and performance analysis” to “Search and content performance optimization” unless SEO is a major selling point elsewhere.
- If space allows, group by function instead of listing tools first: “Measurement strategy • KPI design • Executive dashboards • Behavioral analytics • Search/content performance • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and the NACo bullet about expanding analytics infrastructure; avoid repeating the exact same wording.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and slightly dated versus the more strategic recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize broadcast-quality production leadership and event delivery capabilities already evidenced in the NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more outcome-oriented, senior phrasing: “Broadcast video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations • Post-production editing”
- Consider swapping “Video production and editing” for “Broadcast-quality video production” to better match the in-house studio achievement.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing broad functions (“Livestreaming”) with equipment (“PTZ camera systems”) unless all items are framed consistently.
- If space allows, make it slightly more strategic: “Studio buildout and operations” instead of just “Studio operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies; vary wording or keep only one broad reference.
- This section should not over-repeat older production work already covered in the 2015–2022 NACo entries.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” In this section, make it more concise and category-led, with emphasis on the platforms most tied to recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, prioritize by recency/strength: put **Drupal** first and consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it’s not materially used in recent roles.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use either **CMS platforms** or **Web platforms & CMS**, not both in different sections.
- Consider adding light proficiency cues only if used elsewhere, e.g. **Drupal (advanced)**, to signal depth without turning this into a full bullet.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the platform list already under **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**.
- **Power Pages** also appears adjacent to broader technical skills; avoid repeating the same tools in multiple sections unless one version adds context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior communications/digital strategy CV, this item should emphasize current, relevant implementation strengths and trim older/front-end basics.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around applied capability, not raw languages: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and tag management integrations • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions”
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) and consider removing “jQuery” unless it is actively used in recent work or required for target roles.
- If space allows, add light context tied to recent work: “for Drupal/CMS environments” or “for web operations and campaign platforms.”
- Put the most current/distinctive tools first: “Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • HTML/CSS/JavaScript”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations”); keep one version shorter or more specialized.
- “Google Tag Manager” may also overlap conceptually with analytics/tooling elsewhere; include only if you’ve used it hands-on recently.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps with stronger “workflow automation” positioning elsewhere. Make it more selective and signal what you built or managed, not just the apps you’ve used.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools”
- Prioritize higher-value systems first and group by function: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Cut lower-signal/redundant tools unless central to target roles: remove Basecamp and Trello if they were only occasional-use platforms.
- If space allows, add light context instead of a pure list: “Workflow automation, project coordination, and cross-team collaboration tools: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Microsoft Teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello are similar category tools; listing all four can read as padding rather than depth.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is clear but too bare compared with the rest of the CV. Since email is a major theme in recent roles, this line should signal level of use and strategic relevance, not just list tools.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (email marketing, newsletter operations, audience engagement)”
- If accurate, strengthen further with scope: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • enterprise newsletter operations • audience segmentation • campaign deployment”
- Keep platform names first, then add 2–3 functional keywords to show applied expertise without turning this into a full bullet.
- Use consistent naming/capitalization; “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys” may read cleaner than the slash format.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already better covered in recent NACo experience.
- Don’t repeat generic “multi-channel communications” language already covered in the summary and core competencies.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it duplicates the “Topline Skills” analytics section almost exactly and reads more like keywords than a differentiated technical category. Tighten it and emphasize methods/tools not already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Data & Optimization Tools
- Replace with a cleaner, more technical list: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting
- Consider swapping broad terms like “SEO” and “Dashboarding” for more specific capabilities/tools if accurate, e.g., Search Console, experimentation, reporting
- Keep ordering by strongest/recently evidenced tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; keep one more strategic and this one strictly tool-based
- “Dashboarding” repeats the reporting idea already implied by Power BI and Looker Studio

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles on video, workflows, and digital operations. Make it more execution-focused and distinguish it as the foundational, early-career build phase.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize setup/build work: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows for web, email, social media, and multimedia production.”
- Add concrete scope or outputs if available: website refresh size, livestream/event volume, frequency of video updates, or team support details.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce soft claims like “high-impact”; name deliverables instead: “Produced livestreams and weekly advocacy video updates.”
- Suggested version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social media, and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day coordination for a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing, and the later one on scaling/owning the channel.
- “Strengthening workflows” overlaps with multiple later roles; specify this as initial team/process setup.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and trim generic support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a more specific verb/result, e.g., “produced digital and multimedia content to support policy communications and member engagement.”
- If possible, add scope or output: number of episodes, stakeholders supported, projects coordinated, or audience/reach.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles since the more recent positions already show broader leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with [4], [3], and [2]; keep this item focused on research/program support plus the first podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating general web/email/social responsibilities that are better covered in later, more senior NACo entries.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item is a bit mixed and generic. Since multimedia leadership already appears strongly in recent roles, this section should stay tool-focused and concise rather than repeat production responsibilities.

Suggested edit
- Reframe as software + production capabilities, with the strongest tools first.
- Replace broad phrasing like “Livestream studio workflows” with clearer, resume-style wording.
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier such as “broadcast-quality” or “multi-camera” to sharpen credibility.
